1.explanation: This Node.js script programmatically launches a headless Chrome, runs Lighthouse only on the uses-rel-preconnect audit against the American Express page, and logs out the exact origins Lighthouse is still recommending. By running it once without any <link rel="preconnect"> tags on your page, you’ll see the six new origins right in your console—reproducing the screenshot. You can then add preconnect tags for those origins in your HTML and rerun the same script to confirm whether Lighthouse still flags them.
1.bug_scenario: In the “Preconnect to required origins” audit, Lighthouse continues to recommend new third-party origins—even after you’ve added <link rel="preconnect"> tags for the originally flagged hosts. For example, after preconnecting to nexus.ensighten.com, aexp-static.com, cdaas.americanexpress.com, aug.americanexpress.com and aexp.demdex.net, the audit still shows six additional origins (acquisition-1-qa.americanexpress.com, origin-pqgemapp.americanexpress.com, qicm.americanexpress.com, ds-aksb-a.akamaiedge.net, cx.atdmt.com, bat.bing.com) with potential savings.
